blocks.source: Source: MLS® data from the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® and the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board, compiled by SnapStats®. Rank counts only communities with at least ten homes listed. Falling listings with steady sales mean homes are being absorbed faster; rising listings with steady sales mean more choice for buyers. A sellers’ best bet is a community where homes sell quickly against the number listed; a buyers’ best bet is the reverse. Sales ratio is homes sold divided by homes listed. On the reports’ own scale under 12% is a buyers’ market, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% is a sellers’ market. With fewer than ten homes listed, one sale moves the ratio a long way, so treat it as a rough signal.

blocks.text: Between June 2026 and September 2026, detached houses: listings rose from 25 in June to 30 in September (+20.0%), and it took 5.7% of the city’s 298 sales over the period; condos and townhomes: listings rose from 23 in June to 35 in September (+52.2%), and it took 4.7% of the city’s 558 sales over the period.
The monthly write-ups singled out Murrayville for condos and townhomes in June, September (a sellers’ best bet).

blocks.text: Local rules that affect condo buyers in Murrayville

items.t: Township zoning and plans: Murrayville sits under the Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500. The Murrayville Community Plan is Amendment (Murrayville Community Plan) Bylaw 1988 No. 2661 to the Langley Official Community Plan Bylaw 1979 No. 1842, adopted April 17, 1989; the consolidated plan document records the further Amendment (2025 OCP Update) Bylaw No. 6200, December 1, 2025 — OCP Bylaw No. 6200 was adopted December 1, 2025. The Township's Development Permits page confirms there are currently two designated heritage conservation areas in the Township — the Fort Langley Community Plan and the Murrayville Community Plan — each with heritage guidelines in its plan, and a Heritage Alteration Permit is required before demolition, subdivision or redevelopment in one.

: Township of Langley Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 Amendment (SSMUH) Bylaw No. 6020, adopted November 18, 2024 — eligible lots (inside the Urban Containment Boundary, on both municipal water and sewer, not heritage-designated, not in a Transit-Oriented Area) may have 3 units if 280 m² or smaller, or 4 units if between 280 m² and 4,050 m²; lots larger than 4,050 m² are not eligible, and there is NO 6-plex tier in the Township. A Township secondary suite is capped at 120 m² under Zoning Bylaw s. 102, as amended; R-CL s.
Township taxes: Township of Langley property taxes were due Thursday, July 2, 2026; a 5% penalty applies at midnight July 2, 2026, and a further 5% at midnight September 3, 2026.

blocks.text: Good to know about Murrayville

items.t: Murrayville's attached market was Langley's fastest in September 2026. There is still no Murrayville median to quote: SnapStats publishes medians at community level only.

One complex, two addresses, two build years in print. Autumn Ridge trades under both 22015 and 22025 48 Avenue as a single strata (Plan LMS1087, 130 units in strata per an MLS data sheet), and its year is stated as 1995 on that sheet and 1993 in other listings — search both addresses and verify the year on the Form B, not on either web line.

Murrayville House's unit count checks out two ways — its year does not. The 92-unit figure appears both on an MLS data sheet ("Total Units in Strata: 92") and in the developer's own December 2019 newspaper advertisement ("a boutique collection of only 92 homes"); the year is 2016 in listing brochures and approximately 2017 on the data sheet.

The heritage layer here is Township-confirmed, even where the page's specifics are not. The Township's own Development Permits page confirms Murrayville is one of only two designated heritage conservation areas in the Township (with Fort Langley) and that a Heritage Alteration Permit is required before demolition, subdivision or redevelopment in one.

A directory entry can misstate a townhouse complex as a small apartment building. The directory's "Murrayville — 21937 Avenue" entry states built 1990 and 22 units with apartment-style framing, while listings for the same address record a townhouse complex with unit numbers running into the 1300s — verify form and count on the MLS data sheet and strata plan, not on the directory's summary.
The page's flowing-well claim is unverified.

The community plan is older than the buildings it now governs. The Murrayville Community Plan is Bylaw No. 2661, adopted April 17, 1989, as an amendment to OCP Bylaw 1979 No. 1842 — and its consolidated text now carries the 2025 OCP Update (Bylaw No. 6200, December 1, 2025) in its amendment table, so a plan citation without the amendment history is incomplete for a Murrayville lot.

blocks.text: Good to know about Murrayville Guide

items.t: SSMUH eligibility in the Township is a servicing test, not a slogan (Township SSMUH page). A Murrayville lot needs the Urban Containment Boundary, municipal water AND sewer, no heritage designation and no Transit-Oriented Area status before the 3- or 4-unit count in Bylaw 6020 is even available — test the exact lot, not the neighbourhood.
The hospital is the neighbourhood's anchor (Fraser Health / Township). Langley Memorial Hospital (22051 Fraser Highway) and W.C.

Heritage and flowing wells, carried as the guide page states them, UNVERIFIED as stated. The guide page states part of Murrayville is a heritage conservation area centred on Murray's Corner, that the Traveller's Hotel (1887) is a scheduled heritage property, that Murrayville's is one of only two heritage conservation areas in the Township, and that the South of Murrayville aquifer (Aquifer 51) is one of three where most of the Township's flowing artesian wells are found.

faq.q: Are there more or fewer homes for sale in Murrayville than in June?
faq.a: In Murrayville, listings of houses rose from 25 in June to 30 in September (+20.0%); condos and townhomes rose from 23 in June to 35 in September (+52.2%).

faq.q: How big is Murrayville compared with the rest of Langley?
faq.a: In September 2026, Murrayville held 6.7% of the 449 houses listed in Langley and 5.0% of the 699 condos and townhomes listed in Langley.

faq.q: How many homes sold in Murrayville from June to September 2026?
faq.a: 17 houses and 26 condos and townhomes sold in Murrayville over those 4 months.

faq.q: Who can help me buy or sell in Murrayville?
faq.a: Jared Gibbons, REALTOR® with Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, works across the Fraser Valley and Metro Vancouver. Call or text 604-928-1361 or use the contact form on this site.

faq.q: How do I find out which school serves an address in Murrayville?
faq.a: School catchments are set by address, so use the school district's catchment locator with the exact address. Catchment lines change, so check before you write an offer.

faq.q: How many apartment-condo buildings does Murrayville actually have?
faq.a: A fourth name, Central (22136 49 Ave), is held UNCONFIRMED and is not counted. Everything else named in is townhouse-form.

faq.q: How did Murrayville sell in September 2026?
faq.a: No Murrayville-specific median is published; the community medians (detached $1,345,000; attached $611,000) are whole-Langley figures, not Murrayville's.

faq.q: Is Murrayville in Langley City or the Township?
faq.a: The Township. The Murrayville Community Plan document describes Murrayville as located on both sides of the Fraser Highway immediately east of the City of Langley, and Murrayville is Township of Langley ground — Township Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 and Township tax dates apply, not the City's Zoning Bylaw 2025, No. 3300.

faq.q: Is Cedar Crest Estates a 55+ community — and is it a condo?
faq.a: It is a townhouse complex at 21848 50 Avenue, not an apartment condo, and its age claim is UNCONFIRMED: one current listing calls it a "55+ gated townhouse community" and another listing text calls the same complex a "45+ gated community." Only a 55-or-older bylaw is enforceable under the Strata Property Act in any case (ss. 123.1/123.2) — read the registered bylaws on the Form B before relying on either number.

faq.q: The directory says rentals are not allowed at 21937 48 Avenue — can I rent a unit there?
faq.a: The rental line does not bind you: rental-restriction bylaws have been void province-wide since November 24, 2022. The same directory entry records age restrictions and pets allowed with restrictions, which can still bind — and the complex is townhouse-form on listing evidence, whatever the directory's building framing suggests.

faq.q: Is Cedar Crest Estates a 55+ community?
faq.a: UNCONFIRMED. Listings conflict — one calls it a "55+ gated townhouse community," an earlier one called it "45+," and no registered bylaws were checked. A 45+ bylaw would be void in law in any case; only the Form B and registered bylaws settle it.

faq.q: Is Murrayville in Langley City or the Township?
What should I read before buying a Murrayville townhome?
faq.a: The Form B, the registered bylaws and rules, two years of minutes and the depreciation report.
